intro: も means "this one too": it adds a word to something already said, or to an expectation, and says the same holds for it. Every use grows from that image. Two items both added (AもBも) means both or neither. A question word plus も with a negative says "none of them, not one". A number plus も says the amount itself goes beyond what you would expect.

skills.rule: Put も right after the word that is "also" the case; it replaces は, が and を, and follows any other particle (にも, でも, とも).
skills.explain:
も attaches to the word that is the addition, not to the end of the sentence. 田中さんが来ました。山田さんも来ました。 Mr Yamada is the extra person, so も goes on him. English "too" floats to the end of the clause; Japanese も is pinned to one word, and moving it changes the meaning: 私もコーヒーを飲みます (I, as well as others, drink coffee) versus 私はコーヒーも飲みます (I drink coffee as well as other things).

も takes the place of は, が and を: never write はも, がも or をも in everyday Japanese. Other particles stay and も goes after them: 京都にも行きました, 図書館でも勉強します, 田中さんとも話しました.

The short reply "me too" is 私もです (or 私も), not 私はです.
patterns: [noun] も [predicate]  (replaces は / が / を)
[noun] に / で / と / から + も [predicate]

examples.jp: 私[わたし]{も}学生[がくせい]です。
examples.en: I am a student too.

examples.jp: 妹[いもうと]{も}犬[いぬ]が好[す]きです。
examples.en: My younger sister likes dogs too.

examples.jp: パン{も}買[か]いました。
examples.en: I bought bread as well.

examples.jp: 日曜日[にちようび]に{も}仕事[しごと]があります。
examples.en: I have work on Sundays too.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]で{も}カードが使[つか]えますか。
examples.en: Can I use a card at this shop too?

examples.jp: 山田[やまだ]さんと{も}相談[そうだん]しました。
examples.en: I talked it over with Ms Yamada as well.

contrast.note: は sets a topic and often contrasts it with others ("as for me..."); も says the same thing is true of it as of something else. 私は行きます: I am going (whatever others do). 私も行きます: I am going too.
と joins people doing something together; も adds a second person who does it as well. 田中さんと行きます: I am going with Mr Tanaka. 田中さんも行きます: Mr Tanaka is going too.
を marks the object, but when the object is the "also" item, も replaces を entirely: 本も読みます, not 本をも読みます.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は{も}行[い]きます。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]{も}行[い]きます。
mistakes.note: も replaces は; the two never stack.

mistakes.bad: 肉[にく]を{も}食[た]べます。
mistakes.note: も replaces を as well. をも exists only in stiff written style.

mistakes.bad: 父[ちち]はお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます。母[はは]はお酒[さけ]{も}飲[の]みます。
mistakes.good: 父[ちち]はお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます。母[はは]{も}お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます。
mistakes.note: To say the mother drinks too, も goes on 母. 母はお酒も飲みます means she drinks alcohol as well as other things.

skills.tip: Ask "what is the new item?" and put も on that word, swallowing any は, が or を it had.

skills.rule: AもBも marks each item with も: with a positive verb it means "both A and B", with a negative verb "neither A nor B".
skills.explain:
Each item in the pair takes its own も, and the predicate decides the meaning: 肉も魚も食べます (I eat both meat and fish); 肉も魚も食べません (I eat neither meat nor fish). English needs two different words, both and neither; Japanese uses the same frame and lets the verb settle it.

Any particle other than は, が or を stays in front of each も: 東京にも大阪にも行きました, 田中さんとも山田さんとも話しました. The frame can run to three items (AもBもCも).

Compare AとBも: that means "A and B, also" (adding the pair to something earlier), and AとB without も is a plain, neutral list. When you want to stress "both" or "neither", repeat も on every item.
patterns: A も B も [positive]  "both A and B"
A も B も [negative]  "neither A nor B"
A に も B に も [verb]

examples.jp: 父[ちち]{も}母[はは]{も}元気[げんき]です。
examples.en: My father and my mother are both well.

examples.jp: 肉[にく]{も}魚[さかな]{も}食[た]べません。
examples.en: I eat neither meat nor fish.

examples.jp: この部屋[へや]は夏[なつ]{も}冬[ふゆ]{も}快適[かいてき]です。
examples.en: This room is comfortable in both summer and winter.

examples.jp: 英語[えいご]{も}中国語[ちゅうごくご]{も}話[はな]せません。
examples.en: I can speak neither English nor Chinese.

examples.jp: 京都[きょうと]に{も}奈良[なら]に{も}行[い]きました。
examples.en: I went to both Kyoto and Nara.

contrast.note: AとB is a neutral, complete list; AもBも stresses that each one is included (both) or excluded (neither). AとBも means the pair is added to something mentioned before.
AやB gives examples from a longer list and implies others; AもBも names exactly these items and stresses each.
AはBは sets up a contrast between two items ("A is..., but B is..."); AもBも says the same is true of both.

mistakes.bad: 肉[にく]と魚[さかな]{も}食[た]べません。
mistakes.good: 肉[にく]{も}魚[さかな]{も}食[た]べません。
mistakes.note: For "neither A nor B" each item needs its own も; AとBも means the pair is an addition to something else.

mistakes.bad: 父[ちち]{も}母[はは]が元気[げんき]です。
mistakes.good: 父[ちち]{も}母[はは]{も}元気[げんき]です。
mistakes.note: The second item needs its own も too; a lone が breaks the pair.

mistakes.bad: 兄[あに]{も}姉[あね]{も}結婚[けっこん]しています。
mistakes.good: 兄[あに]{も}姉[あね]{も}結婚[けっこん]していません。
mistakes.note: For "neither my brother nor my sister is married" the verb must be negative; the positive verb says both are married.

skills.tip: Same frame, two meanings: look at the verb ending. Positive means both, negative means neither.

skills.rule: Question word + も + negative verb means "no one / nothing / nowhere"; particles other than が and を go between the question word and も.
skills.explain:
何も, 誰も, どこも, どれも with a negative verb deny every possibility: 何も食べませんでした (I ate nothing), 誰も来ませんでした (no one came). The verb must be negative; English "nothing" sits on the noun, but in Japanese the negation is in the verb.

が and を disappear: 誰も (never 誰がも), 何も (never 何をも). Every other particle stays, before も: どこにも行きません (I am not going anywhere), 誰にも言わないで (do not tell anyone), 誰とも話しませんでした. Leaving out that particle changes the role: 誰も話しませんでした means no one spoke, not that I spoke to no one.

Exceptions that matter: いつも simply means "always" (いつも歩いて行きます), never "at no time". For "anything / anyone" in a positive sentence use でも (何でも, 誰でも). For "something / someone" use か (何か, 誰か). Note the reading: 何も is なにも.
patterns: どこにも / 誰にも / 誰とも [negative]
どれも [negative or positive: "none / all of them"]

examples.jp: 今朝[けさ]は何[なに]{も}食[た]べませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't eat anything this morning.

examples.jp: 教室[きょうしつ]には誰[だれ]{も}いません。
examples.en: There is nobody in the classroom.

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]はどこに{も}行[い]きませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't go anywhere at the weekend.

examples.jp: このことは誰[だれ]に{も}言[い]わないでください。
examples.en: Please don't tell anyone about this.

examples.jp: パーティーでは誰[だれ]と{も}話[はな]しませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't talk to anyone at the party.

contrast.note: Question word + か means "some-": 誰か来ましたか (Did someone come?). Question word + も + negative means "no-": 誰も来ませんでした (No one came). Questions and positives take か; denials take も.
誰が来ましたか asks who came. In the answer "no one", が is replaced: 誰も来ませんでした, never 誰がも.
何でも, 誰でも, どこでも with a positive verb mean "anything / anyone / anywhere at all": 何でも食べます (I eat anything).

mistakes.bad: 何[なに]を{も}買[か]いませんでした。
mistakes.good: 何[なに]{も}買[か]いませんでした。

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]は誰[だれ]{も}電話[でんわ]しませんでした。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]は誰[だれ]に{も}電話[でんわ]しませんでした。
mistakes.note: "I phoned no one": keep the に that 電話する needs. Without it, 誰も is the subject: no one phoned.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は何[なに]{も}食[た]べます。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は何[なん]{でも}食[た]べます。
mistakes.note: Question word + も needs a negative. For "I eat anything" use 何でも (なんでも).

skills.tip: See 何, 誰 or どこ before a blank and the verb ends in -ない or -ません? The answer is も, with any に, と or で kept in front of it.

skills.rule: Amount + も stresses that the amount is surprisingly large; 一 + counter + も (or 少しも) with a negative means "not even one, not at all".
skills.explain:
Put も straight after a number and counter to show the amount goes beyond what you expected: 三時間も待ちました (I waited a full three hours). It adds the speaker's feeling; the fact is the same as 三時間待ちました. With a question word, 何時間も, 何度も, 何人も mean "for hours, again and again, many people", and the verb is positive. This is the trap: 何度も is not a denial.

With one unit and a negative verb, も means "not even one": 一円もありません, 一度も行ったことがありません. 少しも and ちっとも work the same way: 少しも分かりません (I don't understand at all).

Durations and amounts normally take no particle at all, so the choice is between nothing (neutral) and も (emphatic). Do not put を or で on them for this meaning. A larger number with a negative means "not even that much": 十分もかかりません (it doesn't even take ten minutes).
patterns: [number + counter] も [positive]  "as many / as long as"
一[counter] も / 少しも [negative]  "not even one, not at all"

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で一時間[いちじかん]{も}待[ま]ちました。
examples.en: I waited at the station for a whole hour.

examples.jp: 財布[さいふ]に一円[いちえん]{も}ありません。
examples.en: There isn't a single yen in my wallet.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]は一日[いちにち]に五杯[ごはい]{も}コーヒーを飲[の]みます。
examples.en: My older brother drinks as many as five cups of coffee a day.

examples.jp: 何度[なんど]{も}電話[でんわ]しましたが、出[で]ませんでした。
examples.en: I called again and again, but nobody answered.

examples.jp: 北海道[ほっかいどう]には一度[いちど]{も}行[い]ったことがありません。
examples.en: I have never once been to Hokkaido.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の説明[せつめい]は少[すこ]し{も}分[わ]かりませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't understand his explanation at all.

contrast.note: Amount + は gives a minimum: 三時間は待ちました (I waited at least three hours). Amount + も stresses that it was a lot: 三時間も待ちました.
しか + negative says the amount is small: 千円しかありません (I only have 1,000 yen). Amount + も + positive says it is large: 千円もあります (I have a whole 1,000 yen).
Number + で marks a group or total: 三人で行きました (we went as a party of three), 千円で買えます (you can buy it for 1,000 yen). Number + も only adds emphasis to the size.

mistakes.bad: 二時間[にじかん]を{も}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.good: 二時間[にじかん]{も}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.note: A duration takes no を; も attaches to it directly.

mistakes.bad: 質問[しつもん]が一[ひと]つ{も}あります。
mistakes.good: 質問[しつもん]が一[ひと]つ{も}ありません。
mistakes.note: 一 + counter + も means "not even one" and needs a negative verb. For "I have one question" drop も.

mistakes.bad: 何度[なんど]{も}行[い]きませんでした。
mistakes.good: 一度[いちど]{も}行[い]きませんでした。
mistakes.note: 何度も means "many times" and takes a positive verb; for "not once" use 一度も.

skills.tip: Number before the blank: big and surprising with a positive verb, or "one" with a negative verb? Then も.
